A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work on privately finding second-order stationary points. Their complete main texts, algorithms, equations, references, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1 Appendix A.2 to v2 Appendix C.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, theoretical guarantees, and proofs, including a generalization theorem in its appendix. It reports no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical, including its expanded appendices. It reports no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: v1 uses gradient estimates with occasional perturbations to escape saddles. v2 introduces Hessian and Hessian-difference oracles, an anchored Hessian-based escape procedure, per-step escape noise, and count-triggered estimator refreshes (Algorithms 2–4). These substantially change the procedure and its oracle requirements.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or scenarios for empirical training or evaluation. Both analyze the same private smooth nonconvex optimization setting, retaining the appendix discussion of empirical-to-population guarantees.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. The added comparison with Tao et al. concerns theoretical guarantees, not an evaluated baseline set.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, metrics, splits, or evaluation budgets. Revised batch sizes and noise scales are specifications of the theoretical algorithm, covered under M1, T1, and D1.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, or case studies. The expanded appendices supply mathematical proofs rather than supplementary experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changes to concentration inequalities and failure-probability arguments are theoretical developments rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured performance values or empirical result entries. Changes to analytic convergence and sample-complexity bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 replaces v1's borrowed escape lemma with a new Hessian-based escape theorem and supporting proofs, adds Hessian-error and privacy-composition analysis, and replaces Matrix Bernstein with Matrix Azuma in Theorem 2.5. The detailed main bound gains rho-dependent terms and an epsilon <= O(1) restriction, while retaining the headline rate.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.1 retain the SOSP rate matching the FOSP bound but add a central contribution claim: the new escape procedure corrects a flaw in Ganesh et al. and recovers or strengthens its guarantees. v1 claimed an improved rate without this corrective contribution.

C2.justification: v1 Appendix A.1 treats sufficiently accurate gradient estimates as enough for the inherited escape argument. v2 explains the full-batch versus minibatch incompatibility and motivates a Hessian power-method remedy. Section 1.1 also clarifies that the claimed FOSP–SOSP gap concerns the regime where the privacy term dominates.

D1.justification: Algorithms 2–4 and Lemma 3.14 provide substantial new procedural specifications: Hessian sampling, displacement and refresh thresholds, and separate tree and escape noise calibrations. The fixed and adaptive batch-size formulas also acquire explicit Hessian-related terms. These specify the revised algorithm; neither version supplies experimental implementation or hardware information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the contribution around Tao et al. (2025)'s criticism of Ganesh et al., contrasting its 2/5 rate with Ganesh's claimed 3/7 rate. It also adds several related works and discusses Fichtenberger et al.'s matrix mechanism as an alternative to the tree mechanism.

P1.justification: Section 3 is reorganized into a dedicated saddle-escape analysis and a main-algorithm subsection. Several formerly inline proofs move to Appendix B, Appendix A houses escape proofs, and the former Appendix A.2 becomes Appendix C. The introduction also gains substantial corrective framing and mechanism explanations.

P2.justification: v2 adds an escape-procedure pseudocode box, expands the main-algorithm and oracle boxes, and relocates the tree-mechanism box. The single-column visual style remains similar, and neither version contains empirical figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 identifies the gap underlying v1's inherited escape argument and supplies a detailed Hessian-based replacement. However, Theorem 3.4 states a Hessian inequality opposite to the condition used in Appendix A.3, and Appendix B.5 does not justify absorbing the added escape-refresh cost under the stated tau. These inconsistencies leave the central correction and retained sample-complexity guarantee unresolved. The improved transparency and fuller specification therefore do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
